note: mapping_basis=data_labels, no inference in the code->text tie: data/goldberg_2018_escs.py melts SPA.tab with var_name=item and renames nothing; SPEY has no BLOCK_NAMES entry, so the table is named from the lower-cased prefix ('spey'), and live codes SPEY1..SPEY12 ARE the .por column names (core model s3 pattern 1). What SPEY is: the 'Before Age 18' column block of SPA.pdf p.7 'Some Personal Experiences' (12 events each answered twice; the 'Age 18 or Older' block is SPEO1..12, table goldberg_2018_spa_speo, batch_396). Tie to text: .por variable labels, 12/12 labelled, each ending '< age 18' (e.g. SPEY1 'Observed an eclipse of the sun or the moon. < age 18', SPEY12 'Was asked to serve as an officer of a club or organization.< age 18'); .sav (lower-case spey1..12) labels identical 12/12. Labels minus the age suffix and trailing period equal the 12 events printed on SPA.pdf p.7 read top to bottom (page render read), 12/12 in order. text_source=study_materials: item_text is the printed form wording without leader dots; equals the label except SPEY3, where the form adds '(such as a parent, brother or sister, caretaker, or intimate partner)' which the label omits -- the printed wording ships. Option<->resp: .por/.sav value labels identical on all 12 columns, 1='never', 2='1-2 times', 3='3+', agreeing in order with the form's three slanted column headers under BEFORE AGE 18 left to right; option_text ships the printed headers 'NEVER' / 'ONE or TWO TIMES' / 'MORE THAN THAT'. Corroboration: .por per-item x resp counts equal live counts in 36/36 cells (8,260 non-missing rows, 711 ids; live data from the local irw cache populated by table_context.R, no new export), e.g. SPEY1 145/430/115, SPEY6 632/41/3, SPEY8 643/29/0 (no respondent chose 3 on SPEY8 in either source; its printed option row ships anyway). The SPEO columns differ (SPEO1 32/360/308), so the table holds the <18 block. instructions = the instruction sentence plus the italic question printed under the heading, verbatim ('AND' underlined in print, emphasis not reproduced), identical to the SPEO sibling. section_prompt = 'BEFORE AGE 18', the printed column-block header these responses were entered under; it is the only text distinguishing this table from SPEO. instrument = deposit title + section heading (composed). One trivial section_id. Step 3b: dictionary Description ('the spey block. resp 1-3. 711 respondents x 12 items = 8260 responses') matches live (8,260 rows, 711 ids, 12 items, resp 1-3) -- no instrument mismatch. Rights: Goldberg-authored life-events checklist in his own CC0 deposit, not a published instrument; no instrument_rights_register.csv row applies and no restriction located (silence). Processing script data/goldberg_2018_escs.py.
note: mapping_basis=data_labels, no inference in the code->text tie: data/goldberg_2018_escs.py melts SPA.tab with var_name=item and renames nothing; BLOCK_NAMES[("spa","ABILITY")]="talents" routes the family here, so live codes ABILITY1..ABILITY9 ARE the .por column names (core model s3 pattern 1). Tie to text: the .por variable label of each ABILITY column, 9/9 labelled with the bare skill name (ABILITY1 "Verbal ability" .. ABILITY9 "Artistic ability"; .sav identical), matching the 9 skills printed on SPA.pdf p.6 in the same top-to-bottom order (page render read at 110 and 250 dpi). text_source=study_materials: item_text ships the full printed wording (skill name + colon + definition, line wraps joined with single spaces; the bold/italic/underlined skill name is not marked), because the labels carry only the name; all 9 item_text strings and the instructions are exact substrings of pdftotext output for p.6. Step 3b: the same nine skills are printed again on p.10 "Profiling Your Skills" (the PSKILL ranking family, goldberg_2018_spa_skill_proficiency); this table is the p.6 percentile block -- ABILITY carries the percentile value labels, and 0 of 719 complete respondents give nine distinct values, so it is not a ranking. Option<->resp: .por/.sav value labels identical on all 9 columns, 0="0-10%", 1="10-20%" .. 8="80-90%" -- 9 levels, and the form prints exactly 9 bubble columns headed "0 - 10%" .. "80 - 90%" left to right (there is NO 90-100% column on the form; checked on a 250 dpi render of the header). option_text ships the printed headers (with the form spacing "0 - 10%"), resp 0..8. The processing script stores the .por values unchanged (no shift): live per-item x resp counts equal the .por in 81/81 cells (6,535 non-missing rows both, 727 ids; live read from the local irw cache populated by table_context.R, no new export), e.g. ABILITY1 17/27/29/34/59/83/144/171/163, ABILITY9 118/111/89/89/75/62/67/51/64. instructions = the italic question under the heading, verbatim ("BETTER THAN" is capitalised and underlined in print; capitals kept, underline not reproduced). instrument = deposit/booklet title + section heading (composed), same form as batch_394-396 siblings. One trivial section_id. Caveat (form design, not a text defect): the scale tops out at "80 - 90%", so a respondent who does better than more than 90% of people had no exact bubble; the highest level is the top-coded bin. Dictionary Description says "talents"; the form calls them abilities/skills -- naming only, no mismatch. Rights: Goldberg-authored self-rating task in his own CC0 deposit, not a published instrument; no instrument_rights_register.csv row applies and no restriction located (silence). Processing script data/matosaslopez_2022_bars_teaching.py.
note: BLOCKED, no item text shipped. The response table pools two DIFFERENT BARS instruments under the same codes BARS_1..BARS_10. data/matosaslopez_2022_bars_teaching.py states both deposits 'administer the *same* 10-item behaviourally-anchored rating scale' because the ten Spanish column labels match (Introduccion a la asignatura .. Satisfaccion general; the face-to-face file only adds '1.- ' prefixes), and codes each column by keyword match on those labels (a label-keyed rename, so the item<->dimension tie itself is sound). But in a BARS the anchors are the item content, and the anchors differ in every dimension: the blended instrument (Behav Sci 2022 Appendix A) is LMS-centred, e.g. BARS_1 point 1 'Teacher does NOT make an introductory videoconference in the first two weeks of the course, neither posts his/her CV and photo in the LMS; ...', BARS_10 point 1 'Teacher demonstrates knowledge and appropriate management of the LMS resources, using them to make the course more appealing'; the face-to-face instrument (RIFOP 2023 says it is the 2019 JUTLP instrument, Appendix B) reads BARS_1 point 1 'Teacher does NOT present all the key points on the teaching guide at the beginning of the course (syllabus, objectives/competencies, ...)', and its overall-satisfaction scale is built from a different behaviour set ('Teacher does NOT exhibit a recognised knowledge of the field ...'). Live data agrees they are different measures: per-item means blended vs face-to-face are 2.5-3.3 vs 3.8-4.3 on every item (e.g. BARS_8 2.5 vs 4.0, BARS_10 2.6 vs 4.0), 14,359 rows/1,436 ids blended and 8,880 rows/888 ids face-to-face (live read from the local irw cache written by table_context.R; no extra export). One option_text per (item, resp) cannot hold both anchor sets: shipping the blended anchors would join the wrong behavioural description to 8,880 of 23,239 rows (38%), and the counterbalanced-design rule forbids presenting one condition's wording as the item's. Shipping only the dimension names would carry no meaning for resp 1..5 while the anchors are recoverable (the #1770 test). Separate rights point, not the operative block: the face-to-face anchors' originating publication (JUTLP 2019) is CC BY-ND 4.0 and the RIFOP paper CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 ES, i.e. reserved rights, so that half would likely be rights-blocked even after a split; the blended anchors are CC BY 4.0 (Behav Sci). Administered language was Spanish for both; the deposits carry only the ten Spanish dimension labels, and both papers print the anchors in English only. Retry test: NO -- determinate verdict; an unchanged retry reaches the same result. What would have to change: the response table must be split by teaching mode (or the item codes distinguished per instrument). After that, the blended table is extractable from Behav Sci Appendix A (10 images, each 5 anchors, OCR from 960px images; English base with language=Spanish per the fallback, or Spanish dimension labels as item_text with English anchors), and the face-to-face table needs a ruling on the CC BY-ND JUTLP source.
